newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans rally late on Brazil but close lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans rally late on Brazil but close lower.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures rallied in late dealings to close unchanged to slightly lower on reports some meteorologists had amended forecasts for rain in key South American growing regions, traders said.
"Some took rain out of the forecast and (forecast) a faster moving weather front. Some now expect only 1/4 to 1/2 inch," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
But Brazilian traders said there was still time for parched areas to recover and produce normal crops.
Soybeans had traded lower most of the session on ideas weekend rains would satiate thirsty soybean crops.
New crop months were supported by private analytical firm Sparks Companies estimate for 1997 U.S. soybean acreage, traders said.
Sparks pegged planted acreage at 64.5 million acres, slightly below trade expectations for 65 million to 66 million. USDA estimated 1996 soybean planted area at 64.2 million acres.
Soybeans closed steady to 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower with March unchanged at $7.48-1/4.
Commercial buying was noted in futures and options with ADM and Term Commodities said to be key buyers of March.

Louis Dreyfus reportedly bought at least 400 March $7.50 calls at 13-1/2 cents per bushel and another 400 March $7.75 calls at 6-1/2 cents. Traders said Dreyfus also bought at least 400 March $8.00 calls at 3-3/4.
Futures volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's tally of 50,266.
